title: Come to the Waters
backstory: Isaiah's book opened with a nation God said had rebelled against him (Isaiah 1:2). Near its close, God calls out to anyone who is thirsty: come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price (Isaiah 55:1). Then he lifts the curtain on new heavens and a new earth, where the voice of weeping shall be no more heard (Isaiah 65:17-19).

passages.synopsis: God calls out like a merchant in the marketplace, but his goods are free. Everyone who thirsts may come to the waters, and those with no money may buy wine and milk without price. God offers an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies promised to David. His feast is for every hungry soul.

Seek the LORD while he may be found, for he will abundantly pardon. His thoughts and ways are higher than ours, as the heavens are higher than the earth. His word is like rain and snow that water the earth, and it never returns to him empty. His people will go out with joy, and the mountains will break into singing.

The Spirit of the Lord rests on God's anointed one, who brings good tidings to the meek. He binds up the brokenhearted and proclaims liberty to the captives. He gives beauty for ashes and the oil of joy for mourning. Centuries later, Jesus read these very words in Nazareth and said they were being fulfilled.

God promises to create new heavens and a new earth, where former troubles are not remembered. Weeping will be heard no more, and his people will enjoy the work of their hands. Before they even call, God will answer. The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and nothing will hurt or destroy in all his holy mountain.

triviaQuestions.question: Who does Isaiah invite to come to the waters?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Isaiah 55:1 — "Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price."

triviaQuestions.question: How much higher are God's ways than our ways?
options: As the heavens are higher than the earth
As a mountain above a valley
As an eagle above its nest
As a king above his servants
triviaQuestions.explanation: Isaiah 55:9 — "For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts."

triviaQuestions.question: What shall the mountains and the hills do when God's people go out with joy?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Isaiah 55:12 — "For ye shall go out with joy, and be led forth with peace: the mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, and all the trees of the field shall clap their hands."

triviaQuestions.question: In God's new earth, which two animals shall feed together?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Isaiah 65:25 — "The wolf and the lamb shall feed together, and the lion shall eat straw like the bullock: and dust shall be the serpent’s meat. They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain, saith the LORD."

hangmanWords.hint: God promised an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of this king
This tree shall come up instead of the brier
In the new earth it shall feed together with the lamb
Like God's word, it comes down from heaven and waters the earth

reflection: God invites everyone who thirsts to come without money and without price. What are you thirsty for that only God can satisfy?
